Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS! 2988 -1980 

3. Material — The keys (excluding handle) shall be made from suitable steels which after heat 
treatment meet the requirements of testing torque and hardness laid down in 2 and 4 respectively, 

4. Hardness — The keys shall be hardened at the square end and the hardness measured at any 
point on the square shall be 390 to 530 HV ( 40 to 50 HRC approximately ). 

5. Requirements — The keys shall be manufactured from bars and finished smooth all over. All 
sharp corners shall be removed. The key shall be free from burrs, cracks, seams or other 
manufacturing defects. 

5-1 The handles of the keys shall conform to Type A of 13:6002-1971 'Specification for tommy 
bars for box spanners \ 

6. Torque Test — For the purpose of the torque test, a rigidly held steel block having a square 
hole of the same size of square as the key, with a tolerance of D12 shall be used. The depth of the 
hole in the block shall be about 2 mm less than dimension U ( see 2 ). The square end of the key 
shall be inserted into the hole to the maximum extent possible and the appropriate torque as given 
in 2 shall be applied at the handles. The application of the torque shall be gradual and without jerks. 
At the completion of the test, the key shall not show any sign of dam.age or deformation. 

7. Designation — Keys for lathe chucks shall be designated by the size of square and number of 

this standard. 

Example: 

A key having a size of square 8 mm shall be designated as: 
Lathe Chuck Key 8 IS : 2989 

8. Marking — Each key for lathe chuck shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the size of 
square( s ) and the manufacturer* s name, initials or trade-mark. 

8.1 IS/ Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

9. Sampling 

9.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser, the procedure given In 
IS : 2500 ( Part i ) -1973 * Sampling inspection tables: Part I inspection by attributes and by count 
of defects (first revision )\ shall be followed for sampling inspection* For various characteristics, 
the sampling plan as given in 9.1.1 and 9.1-2 shall be followed, 

9.1.1 For inspection for dimensions and visual examination, the single sampling plan with 
inspection level IV and acceptable quality level ( AQL ) 4 percent given in Tables 1 and 2 of IS : 2500 
( Part I )-1973 shall be followed. 

9.1.2 For torque test, th^ sampling plan with inspection level I and acceptable quality level 
( AQL ) 2'5 percent given In Tables 1 and 2 of lb : 2500 ( Part I )-1973 shall be followed. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1965. In this revision, the dimensions and the testing 
torque values have been modified and reference to IS: 6002-1971 'Specification for tommy bars for 
box spanners' has been made for requirements for handles of the keys. 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from DIN 905-1967 ' Vierkant- 
Einsteckschiussel'r< Male square tee wrenches ) issued by Deutsches Institutfiir Normung ( DIN ).
